new.title: Approximations
sample: This topic was split out of **Simplification** so that approximation can be practised on its own. Its paper counts are in that topic's Quick revision tab: in the sample, approximation appeared in one IBPS Clerk paper (the 2017 model, 4 questions) and in each IBPS PO Prelims paper as a block of five; never in SBI Clerk or RRB Clerk.
revision: **One routine:** round every number to a friendly one, solve the tidy question, pick the nearest option.
**Options close together:** round less; keep whole numbers and check the biggest rounding.
**Traps.** Rounding a divisor so that it no longer divides cleanly. Rounding 47 to 50 under a square. Forgetting the order of operations after rounding.

intro: Approximation is Simplification with one step in front: **round first, then calculate**. The numbers are chosen to sit a whisker from round ones.
There are six short lessons. The first is taken from Simplification; the other five fill in each kind of term and how to read the options.
What the papers ask (Simplification Stage A count and the sister papers, all memory-based):
| IBPS Clerk Prelims, 22 papers | 4, all in the 2017 model paper (Seen once) |
| IBPS PO Prelims, 4 papers | a block of five in each |
| SBI Clerk and IBPS RRB Clerk, 8 papers | none |
So give this topic less time than Simplification for Clerk Prelims, and more if you are also sitting PO.
after: That is the whole topic. The **Quick revision** tab has the rounding table.
Everything here leans on Simplification; if a tidy question still feels slow, go back to that topic's lessons.

lessons.title: Approximation
lessons.plain: New: the numbers are ugly on purpose, such as 24.98 and 119.97. Round each to a friendly number first, then solve.
teach: Some questions ask for the **approximate** value. You can tell them by the numbers: 24.98, 16.02, 119.97. Each is a whisker away from a round number, and that is the hint. Nobody is expected to multiply 24.98 by 16.02.
The method is one step added to everything you already know:
1. **Round every number to the nearest friendly value.** 24.98 becomes 25. 16.02 becomes 16. 119.97 becomes 120.
2. **Solve the tidy question** exactly as usual.
3. **Choose the option nearest to your answer.** It will usually match exactly.
A few things to round with care.
- **Percents**: round to one you can do. 34.98% is 35%. 33.32% is one third. 16.67% is one sixth.
- **Roots**: round the number under the root to the nearest perfect square or cube. √624.9 is √625 = 25. ∛342.9 is ∛343 = 7.
- **A root that is not a perfect square**, such as √255: use the nearest one, √256 = 16.
Do not round too early or too roughly. Change each number by a tiny amount only; if you find yourself turning 31.98 into 30, you have gone too far. It should become 32.
One oddity: if the blank is squared, a paper may give the answer as ± 12, meaning 12 or minus 12, since both give 144 when squared.

tags: A real paper: squares, a blank that is squared, and a root that is not exact.

lessons.title: Round, then the usual order
lessons.plain: New: longer chains of multiplying, dividing, adding and subtracting.
teach: Round every number first, then follow the usual order: brackets, then division and multiplication from left to right, then addition and subtraction.
**Round to a number that divides cleanly.** 1439.89 / 11.99: round to 1440 / 12 = 120, not 1400 / 12.
**Several divisions in a row** go left to right: 1400 / 35 / 8 x 20 = 40 / 8 x 20 = 100.

tags: A cube in disguise: 2197 = 13 x 13 x 13.
A real paper (2017 model): left to right.

lessons.title: Percents and fractions
lessons.plain: New: percent and fraction terms, which hide easy fractions.
teach: Round the percent to a friendly one and use its fraction:
| Percent | Fraction |
**Same base, add the percents first.** 39.98% of 650 + 59.97% of 650 = 100% of 650.
A fraction of a number: round the number so the fraction divides it. 3/7 of 489.97 becomes 3/7 of 490 = 210.

example.answer: 24 (IBPS PO Prelims 24 Aug 2025 Shift 1, memory-based; key 24).

check.why: A quarter of 1,200 is 300 and a sixth of 360 is 60: 360. (300 forgets the second term.)

lessons.title: Squares, cubes and roots that are nearly exact
lessons.plain: New: a number just off a perfect square or cube.
teach: Know the squares to 30 and the cubes to 15; then a near number is easy:
| Looks like | Use |
Inside a root, round each part, finish the inside, then take the root: √(16 x 25 + 41) = √441 = 21.

tags: A root that is not quite exact.
A cube root times a square root.

lessons.title: When the blank is inside
lessons.plain: New: the question mark is not alone after the equals sign.
teach: Round everything, then **undo** the steps around the blank, the way you would in Simplification.
| The blank is | Undo by |
Collect the known terms on one side first, then undo the last operation done to the blank.

lessons.title: Let the options set the precision
lessons.plain: New: how much to round depends on how far apart the options are.
teach: Before rounding, glance at the options.
- **Options far apart** (45, 50, 41, 47, 43 are close; 30, 45, 20, 25, 50 are far): round boldly to whole tens.
- **Options close together** (805, 800, 815, 840, 865): keep whole numbers, and do not round 249.11 to 250 and 128.97 to 130 in the same sum without checking the total error.
- When two options are both near your answer, round less and redo the step that moved the most.
In the sample, these questions came only in IBPS PO Prelims, as a block of five per paper. The Clerk papers checked had approximation only in one 2017 model paper.
